originalTitle: CNBC's The China Connection newsletter: A U.S.-China debate that's becoming bigger than tariffs
summary: The AI race is heating up so fast this summer that it's reshaping national priorities in the U.S. and China.
content:
Hi, this is Evelyn, writing to you from Beijing. Welcome to the latest edition of The China Connection — a snapshot of what I'm seeing and hearing from local businesses.

As Chinese startups build new artificial intelligence models and more American startups use them, they're raising the stakes for U.S.-China relations.

China's role in AI is transforming rapidly.

President Xi Jinping's AI speech on July 17 and the coinciding release of Claude Fable 5 rival Kimi K3 were just a start. The flurry of U.S. government pushback on Chinese open-source models ignited calls against " premature restrictions " in an open letter Friday from Nvidia's Jensen Huang and more than 20 other tech companies.

"To me, the release of Kimi K3 has kicked off a hornet's debate in Washington about what to do about Chinese open-weight models," said Ryan Fedasiuk, fellow at the American Enterprise Institute.

The debate will soon be tested at a high level.

In remarks late last week about a U.S. data center policy , U.S. President Donald Trump said he plans to discuss AI with Xi during a visit to the U.S. in late September. China's foreign ministry responded by saying Beijing was ready to work with the U.S. on AI .

Whether the two countries end up being more collaborative — or adversarial — on the technology will be "very consequential," said Lex Zhao, a Chinese-born venture capitalist who oversees $150 million in assets as a Boston-based managing partner at One Way Ventures.

"The reality is that a lot of American startups use Chinese AI models," he said. "A lot of companies we invest in build on top of these models."

Zhao believes the U.S. and China each hold "a lot of leverage" over the other, limiting what actions they will take on AI.

Such commercial interdependence is turning a technology challenge for Washington into a diplomatic one.

This month, China not only hosted its World AI Conference in Shanghai but also the APEC Digital Weeks in Chengdu , where nearly two dozen senior tech officials gathered — including from the U.S.

George Chen, partner and chair of digital practice at consultancy The Asia Group, attended both events.

"Now Beijing also views AI as a new kind of diplomacy to grab more allies and partners," he said, adding that the coming Trump-Xi summit in Washington, D.C., in September will be the first time the two leaders can address AI diplomacy matters.

China's tech advances have come despite four years of U.S. restrictions on access to advanced semiconductors for training AI. Excitement over powerful new models is still constrained by computing power.

Earlier this month, AI consultant Shu Weibing said he visited Z.ai 's offices, only to find a three-month waitlist for companies wanting to use the startup's most advanced GLM 5.2 coding tools released in mid-June. Z.ai did not respond to a request for comment.

And just a few days after Moonshot launched Kimi K3, the startup said it was pausing new subscriptions due to computing power limits.

China is pouring resources into domestic computing capabilities. Z.ai is ramping up a giant 1-gigawatt data center, a source familiar with the matter confirmed to CNBC.

But the pace of Chinese AI releases, even as of late June, convinced slightly more Americans that China is more advanced than the U.S. on developing AI, according to a Pew Research survey. A separate Pew study in early July found that roughly half of Americans disagreed with both Democratic and Republican policies related to AI.

U.S.-based Hugging Face even said it had to use Z.ai's GLM 5.2 to address a cyberattack from a rogue OpenAI model.

"The incident clearly underscores why open source is so necessary for American enterprise and it would be foolish to close it off," said Fedasiuk, noting "I think it's possible to stake out a middle ground here."

Amid U.S. companies' claims that Chinese developers stole AI capabilities, the most advanced U.S. open-source model to date, from startup Thinking Machines Lab, disclosed that it used DeepSeek and Kimi in the development process.

Other countries are watching closely. APEC representatives gathered in Chengdu published a statement Thursday in support of open-source AI models "that employ strong security assurance ."

It's not clear whether policy, even if discussed by the leaders of the world's two largest economies in two months' time, can secure an edge in the fast-moving AI race.

The best practice among businesses is to use systems that give them the option to switch between different models, rather than just relying on one, said One Way's Zhao.

As Chinese models improve and spread, it may become harder for companies in the U.S. and elsewhere not to build on them.

Geely to make EVs at Ford plant in Spain under new joint venture

The joint venture is expected to include a new electric crossover for Ford , in "addition to a new member of the Bronco family, plus two electric Geely SUVs, with production starting in 2028," the companies said. In China, car sales are headed for their worst year since 2021 as growth slows.

Industrial profit growth slows again in June

China's industrial profits rose by 15.1% in June from a year earlier, down from May's 21.1% gain. Investors will now turn to the Communist Party's Politburo meeting, traditionally held in late July, where economists anticipate stronger easing language after the second-quarter slowdown.

Memory chipmaker CXMT skyrockets 470% in Shanghai debut

The Hefei-based company raised 57.92 billion yuan ($8.6 billion) after pricing its IPO at 8.66 yuan per share. Shares surged to 49 yuan apiece on open. CXMT held a 7.67% share of the global DRAM market in 2025, based on fourth-quarter sales figures shared in its IPO prospectus.

chineseTitle: CNBC 的《中国连线》时事通讯：一场比关税更重要的美中辩论
chineseSummary: 今年夏天，人工智能竞赛升温得如此之快，以至于它正在重塑美国和中国的国家优先事项。
chineseContent:
你好，我是伊芙琳，从北京给你写信。欢迎阅读最新一期的《中国连线》——我从当地企业看到和听到的情况的快照。

随着中国初创企业建立新的人工智能模型，并且越来越多的美国初创企业使用它们，它们正在提高中美关系的风险。

中国在人工智能领域的角色正在迅速转变。

习近平主席 7 月 17 日的人工智能讲话以及同期发布的《克劳德寓言 5》的竞争对手 Kimi K3 只是一个开始。美国政府对中国开源模式的一系列抵制引发了英伟达 (Nvidia) 黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 和其他 20 多家科技公司在周五的公开信中反对“过早限制”的呼声。

美国企业研究所研究员 Ryan Fedasiuk 表示：“对我来说，Kimi K3 的发布在华盛顿引发了关于如何处理中国开放重量模型的激烈辩论。”

这场辩论很快将在高层进行考验。

美国总统唐纳德·特朗普在上周晚些时候关于美国数据中心政策的讲话中表示，他计划在 9 月底访问美国期间与习近平讨论人工智能问题。中国外交部回应称，北京已准备好与美国在人工智能领域开展合作。

出生于中国的风险投资家、波士顿 One Way Ventures 管理合伙人莱克斯·赵 (Lex Zhu) 表示，两国最终在技术上是否会加强合作，还是对抗，都将“非常重要”。

“现实情况是，很多美国初创公司都在使用中国的人工智能模型，”他说。 “我们投资的许多公司都是建立在这些模型之上的。”

赵认为，美国和中国都对对方拥有“很大的影响力”，限制了他们在人工智能方面采取的行动。

这种商业上的相互依赖正在将华盛顿面临的技术挑战转变为外交挑战。

本月，中国不仅在上海举办了世界人工智能大会，还在成都举办了亚太经合组织数字周，近二十名高级科技官员聚集一堂，其中包括来自美国的官员。

咨询公司 The Asia Group 合伙人兼数字业务主席 George Chen 出席了这两项活动。

他说：“现在北京也将人工智能视为一种新型外交，以争取更多盟友和合作伙伴。”他补充说，即将于 9 月在华盛顿特区举行的特朗普与习近平峰会将是两位领导人首次讨论人工智能外交问题。

尽管美国四年来一直限制使用先进半导体来训练人工智能，但中国的技术仍然取得了进步。对强大的新模型的兴奋仍然受到计算能力的限制。

本月早些时候，人工智能顾问舒卫兵表示，他参观了再爱科技的办公室，结果发现，想要使用该初创公司 6 月中旬发布的最先进的 GLM 5.2 编码工具的公司已经有了三个月的等待名单。 Z.ai 没有回应置评请求。

就在 Moonshot 推出 Kimi K3 几天后，这家初创公司表示，由于计算能力限制，它将暂停新的订阅。

中国正在向国内计算能力投入资源。一位知情人士向 CNBC 证实，Z.ai 正在扩建一个 1 吉瓦的巨型数据中心。

但皮尤研究中心的一项调查显示，即使截至 6 月底，中国人工智能发布的速度也让稍微多一点的美国人相信，中国在人工智能开发方面比美国更先进。皮尤研究中心 7 月初的另一项研究发现，大约一半的美国人不同意民主党和共和党与人工智能相关的政策。

美国的 Hugging Face 甚至表示必须使用 Z.ai 的 GLM 5.2 来应对来自流氓 OpenAI 模型的网络攻击。

费达西克表示：“这一事件清楚地凸显了为什么开源对于美国企业如此必要，而关闭它是愚蠢的。”他指出，“我认为可以在这里找到一个中间立场。”

在美国公司声称中国开发者窃取了美国迄今为止最先进的开源模型人工智能能力的情况下，初创公司 Thinking Machines Lab 透露，该公司在开发过程中使用了 DeepSeek 和 Kimi。

其他国家正在密切关注。亚太经合组织代表周四齐聚成都发表声明，支持“采用强有力的安全保证”的开源人工智能模型。

目前尚不清楚，即使世界最大的两个经济体的领导人在两个月的时间内讨论了政策，是否能够在快速发展的人工智能竞赛中获得优势。

One Way 的赵说，企业的最佳实践是使用可以在不同模型之间切换的系统，而不是仅仅依赖一种模型。

随着中国模式的改进和传播，美国和其他地方的公司可能会更难不以中国模式为基础。

吉利将通过新合资企业在西班牙福特工厂生产电动汽车

两家公司表示，该合资企业预计将包括福特的一款新型电动跨界车，“此外还有 Bronco 家族的新成员，以及两款电动吉利 SUV，将于 2028 年开始生产”。在中国，随着增长放缓，汽车销量将迎来 2021 年以来最糟糕的一年。

6月份工业利润增速再次放缓

6月份中国工业利润同比增长15.1%，低于5月份21.1%的增幅。投资者现在将转向传统上于 7 月下旬举行的共产党政治局会议，经济学家预计，第二季度经济放缓后，会上将出现更强硬的宽松政策。

存储芯片制造商长鑫存储上海上市暴涨470%

这家总部位于合肥的公司将 IPO 定价为每股 8.66 元人民币，筹集了 579.2 亿元人民币（合 86 亿美元）。开盘后股价飙升至每股49元。根据IPO招股说明书中分享的第四季度销售数据，长鑫存储将在2025年占据全球DRAM市场7.67%的份额。
